title: features/link/serve.feature and browser.feature with serve.rs tests and web/test/link-clock.test.ts (red first)
description:
## Intent
Write M3's stories as specs and watch them fail.

Stories: apricitus-79d979, apricitus-1ba752, apricitus-0afc13.

## Steps
1. `features/link/serve.feature` and `features/link/browser.feature`, the Gherkin verbatim, each headed by where its scenarios are implemented (the `features/serve/serve.feature` convention).
2. Rust tests in `crates/apricity-cli/src/serve.rs` named after the serve scenarios, on a `ScriptedSession`.
3. `web/test/link-clock.test.ts` (node test via `tsx --test`, added to `test:flow` in `web/package.json`): scripted clock stream, fake `AudioContext` timestamps, and the wasm mixer for the audible checks.
4. Watch every test fail for the missing behavior.

## Verify
`cargo test -p apricity-cli serve` and `cd web && npx tsx --test test/link-clock.test.ts` fail on the new cases (paste the summary).

Commit: with the implementing tasks, or `test(<this task id>)`.

## Protocol
Specs first, watched red; log decisions, problems and outcomes with `kbs comment`; run Verify and paste the tail. Every Bash call starts `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH && cd /Users/home/Projects/Apricity`; cargo with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` under `safe-run.sh --`. Never change dependencies to make a build pass. Sub-agents never commit, push or close.
